correctness.rationale: Exact Lagrange-coefficient upper bound reduces the full joint density to N−1 integrable one-dimensional chord factors whenever beta−2p>−1; a separated two-point collision and explicit Rayleigh vector force divergence for beta−2p≤−1. Conditional Gaussian moments sandwich the observed squared error between positive multiples of T^p. Cofactor orthogonality and explicit N=2 gamma integration verify normalization independently; companion code executed all 70 checks. No finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

evidence: General volume-sampling Lemma 4.9 controls only a first inverse-Gram matrix expectation; Tucci–Whiting assumes iid nodes for asymptotics.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General Fourier-sampling risk bounds, determinant sampling and classical circular-beta densities were examined for a direct stronger theorem. Published first-moment and iid statements do not dominate the all-beta all-fractional-p two-sided equivalence, particularly the variance failure at beta=2. Residual incomplete coverage is listed separately.

evidence: Tucci–Whiting Theorem 3.3 covers divergence for iid spectral moments p≥1.
Nouy–Michel Lemma 4.9 covers the beta=2 first moment as a special case of general projection-volume sampling.
Xu–Shen analyze iid uniform/jittered/equidistant but not joint circular-beta density.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Covered implications are removed from novelty: the iid integer divergence and the beta=2 matrix first moment are credited. The surviving single theorem is the beta-dependent necessary and sufficient range for every p>0 and bounded positive density perturbations, together with its conditional Gaussian-noise equivalence; none of the cited stronger statements entails both boundary sides for general beta.

evidence: Tucci–Whiting, Theorem 3.3, proves iid integer-order inverse spectral divergence; the node density has no Vandermonde repulsive power.
Nouy–Michel, Lemma 4.9, supplies first inverse-Gram mean for projection DPP, but no sharp full moment spectrum.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The norm trace \(T\) is equivalent at fixed dimension to minimum-singular-value negative powers for moment finiteness. This implication was checked against earlier iid inverse-moment results. The independent result does not imply the beta-dependent existence regime; first DPP mean cannot imply finite or infinite higher fractional moments.

evidence: The inspected original works present mean-risk expressions, inverse Vandermonde formulas and DPP sampling laws, not a finite-N exact table of critical exponents.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: This is a continuous beta/p finiteness classification rather than a finite integer lookup or a parameter tabulation. No exact table found in the checked primary sources resolves the statement; search absence alone is not a proof of novelty.

originality.rationale: Compared full primary literature on iid random Fourier risk, iid negative Vandermonde spectral moments and determinantally sampled least squares. The iid divergence and beta=2 first-moment cofactor identity are explicitly credited, not included in the novelty claim; no inspected material implies the complete arbitrary-beta fractional threshold with density-perturbation robustness. Historical priority remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently established; an older specialized circular-ensemble inverse-interpolation result could exist outside inspected sources.
The exact unitary inverse-Gram first moment follows from published projection-volume-sampling identities and is deliberately not asserted to be original.
No independent mathematical audit of the general beta-moment proof has occurred.
The two-sided boundedness of G and the square consecutive Fourier band cannot be weakened without a separate theorem.

value.rationale: The exact moment spectrum resolves the natural rare-node-collision obstruction to random Fourier interpolation risk, separates existence of mean squared risk from its variance and gives sharp beta=1 and beta=3 thresholds independent of interpolation dimension. It is motivated by recent risk-divergence results and makes a structurally useful distinction among standard circular repulsion ensembles, not merely an arbitrary finite computation.
